core.text: When working on a team project, I typically:

options.a: Take charge and direct the group toward the goal
options.b: Make sure everyone feels included and valued
options.c: Create a detailed plan and keep us on schedule
options.d: Keep the energy high and momentum moving

core.text: When a deadline is approaching, I:

options.a: Push hard to make sure we hit the mark
options.b: Check in with everyone to see how they are holding up
options.c: Review the plan and adjust priorities as needed
options.d: Find a way to make the final push feel exciting

core.text: When conflict arises in a group, I tend to:

options.a: Address it head-on and push for a quick resolution
options.b: Listen to all sides and help everyone feel understood
options.c: Identify the root cause and propose a structured solution
options.d: Lighten the tension and redirect the group toward common ground

core.text: When planning a celebration for someone, I:

options.a: Take the lead and make the key decisions to get it done
options.b: Focus on making it personal and meaningful to them
options.c: Organize every detail so nothing is left to chance
options.d: Go all out to make it fun and memorable

core.text: When someone gives me feedback on my work, I:

options.a: Want it to be direct and to the point
options.b: Appreciate when it comes with warmth and care
options.c: Want specific examples and actionable suggestions
options.d: Prefer an encouraging tone that keeps me motivated

core.text: When I need to make a decision quickly, I:

options.a: Trust my instincts and act decisively
options.b: Consider how it will affect the people involved
options.c: Gather the key facts before committing
options.d: Go with whatever feels most exciting and bold

core.text: When I meet someone for the first time, I:

options.a: Get to the point and find out what they are about
options.b: Focus on making them feel comfortable and welcome
options.c: Ask thoughtful questions to understand their background
options.d: Look for ways to make the conversation lively and fun

core.text: When I face a major setback, I:

options.a: Regroup fast and find the next path forward
options.b: Lean on people I trust to process it together
options.c: Analyze what went wrong so I can prevent it next time
options.d: Push through with optimism and look for a new opportunity

core.text: During a brainstorming session, I:

options.a: Drive the group toward the most viable idea quickly
options.b: Make sure quieter voices get a chance to contribute
options.c: Take notes and evaluate each idea against our goals
options.d: Throw out bold, unconventional ideas to spark creativity

core.text: When plans change unexpectedly, I:

options.a: Take control of the situation and pivot the strategy
options.b: Check on how the change is affecting everyone
options.c: Work out a revised plan before moving forward
options.d: Embrace the change and look for the upside in it

core.text: When I am leading a discussion, I:

options.a: Keep things focused and steer toward outcomes
options.b: Create space for everyone to share and be heard
options.c: Follow a clear agenda and stay on topic
options.d: Keep it engaging and make sure energy stays high

core.text: When tackling a long, complex task, I:

options.a: Charge through it with a focus on getting it done
options.b: Work alongside others to keep the connection strong
options.c: Break it into steps and check each one off systematically
options.d: Find ways to make the process enjoyable along the way

core.text: When someone comes to me upset, I:

options.a: Help them identify the problem and figure out next steps
options.b: Sit with them and make sure they feel fully heard
options.c: Ask clarifying questions to understand the situation fully
options.d: Try to lift their spirits and help them see the bright side

core.text: When entering a new environment, I:

options.a: Establish my presence and figure out how things work
options.b: Look for people to connect with and build relationships
options.c: Observe carefully before making any moves
options.d: Dive in enthusiastically and bring positive energy

core.text: When setting goals for the year, I:

options.a: Set ambitious targets and commit to achieving them
options.b: Think about the relationships and people I want to invest in
options.c: Build a clear roadmap with milestones and timelines
options.d: Dream big and pick goals that genuinely excite me

core.text: When I am under significant pressure, I:

options.a: Focus harder and channel the pressure into performance
options.b: Stay grounded by staying connected to the people around me
options.c: Go back to the plan and work through it step by step
options.d: Keep a positive attitude and encourage those around me

core.text: When the team achieves a major win, I:

options.a: Acknowledge it briefly and start thinking about the next goal
options.b: Make sure everyone who contributed feels recognized
options.c: Review what worked so we can repeat it
options.d: Celebrate loudly and let the moment be as big as possible

core.text: When given a challenging assignment, I:

options.a: Accept it with confidence and figure out how to win
options.b: Think about who I can partner with to do it well
options.c: Research it thoroughly before I begin
options.d: Get energized by the challenge and jump in

core.text: When preparing for an important conversation, I:

options.a: Think through my key points and what outcome I want
options.b: Consider how the other person is feeling and what they need
options.c: Write out what I want to say so I am fully prepared
options.d: Trust myself to read the room and keep it authentic

core.text: When a project loses momentum, I:

options.a: Identify who needs to step up and push things forward
options.b: Have one-on-ones to find out what is stopping people
options.c: Revisit the plan and find where things went off track
options.d: Rally the team with fresh energy and a new perspective

core.text: When starting something from scratch, I:

options.a: Define the vision and get moving as fast as possible
options.b: Bring people in early so we build it together
options.c: Lay a solid foundation before anything else
options.d: Get excited about the possibilities and inspire others to join

core.text: The way I prefer to communicate with others is:

options.a: Direct, clear, and results-focused
options.b: Warm, genuine, and attentive to how they are feeling
options.c: Precise, organized, and thorough
options.d: Upbeat, expressive, and enthusiastic

currency.text: When someone wants to show me they care, I most appreciate when they:

options.a: Tell me what they love about me or what I mean to them
options.b: Do something helpful for me without me having to ask
options.c: Give me a thoughtful gift, even something small
options.d: Set aside dedicated time to be fully present with me
options.e: Offer a warm hug, a hand on the shoulder, or physical closeness

currency.text: After a really hard day, I feel most comforted when someone:

options.a: Tells me they are proud of me and that I handled it well
options.b: Takes something off my plate so I can rest
options.c: Brings me something to make the evening special
options.d: Sits with me and just listens without distractions
options.e: Gives me a long hug or stays physically close

currency.text: I feel most celebrated on my birthday when:

options.a: People say heartfelt things about what I mean to them
options.b: Someone handles everything so I do not have to worry
options.c: I receive a gift that shows they really know me
options.d: We spend the whole day together doing what I enjoy
options.e: There is lots of physical warmth, hugs, and togetherness

currency.text: The thing that makes me feel most connected to a close friend is:

options.a: When they regularly remind me why I matter to them
options.b: When they show up and help without needing to be asked
options.c: When they remember small things and honor them with a gesture
options.d: When we carve out uninterrupted time just for each other
options.e: When they greet me warmly and are physically affectionate

currency.text: When I do something well, I feel most recognized when:

options.a: Someone tells me specifically what I did right
options.b: Someone steps in to help me with the next thing I need
options.c: I receive something tangible to mark the moment
options.d: Someone wants to take me out or spend time with me to celebrate
options.e: I get a congratulatory hug or a pat on the back

currency.text: In a romantic relationship, I feel most loved when my partner:

options.a: Consistently expresses their feelings and appreciation verbally
options.b: Handles things for me to make my life easier
options.c: Surprises me with something they picked out just for me
options.d: Gives me their full, undivided attention regularly
options.e: Is physically affectionate and initiates touch often

currency.text: When I am going through something difficult, I feel most supported when someone:

options.a: Speaks words of encouragement and belief into me
options.b: Quietly handles practical needs I have not even voiced
options.c: Gives me something meaningful to remind me I am not alone
options.d: Stays with me and gives me their full time and attention
options.e: Holds my hand or keeps physical contact to ground me

currency.text: When I express love to someone important to me, I naturally tend to:

options.a: Say it clearly and often with sincere words
options.b: Look for ways to make their life easier or lighter
options.c: Find or create something thoughtful to give them
options.d: Plan dedicated time together that is just about them
options.e: Be physically close, affectionate, and present

currency.text: I notice I feel emotionally distant in a relationship when:

options.a: Words of appreciation and affirmation are rarely spoken
options.b: I feel like I am carrying everything on my own
options.c: There are no gestures or tokens that show they were thinking of me
options.d: We keep getting interrupted or distracted when we are together
options.e: There is little to no physical connection between us

currency.text: When a friend or partner goes out of their way for me, the gesture that means the most is:

options.a: A handwritten note telling me exactly how much they value me
options.b: Taking care of something I have been stressed about
options.c: Bringing me something they picked specifically because of me
options.d: Clearing their schedule to spend the day together
options.e: Pulling me in for a hug and not letting go too quickly

currency.text: When I am feeling insecure or unsure, what helps me most is:

options.a: Someone speaking truth and affirmation over me directly
options.b: Someone stepping in and taking action to help me
options.c: Receiving something tangible that reminds me I am valued
options.d: Having a long, unrushed conversation with someone I trust
options.e: Being held or having someone physically close to me

currency.text: On an ordinary day with no special occasion, I feel most cherished when:

options.a: I get an unexpected text or note saying what I mean to someone
options.b: Someone does something helpful for me without being prompted
options.c: I receive a small surprise, something simple but intentional
options.d: We spend time together that is unhurried and just ours
options.e: There is consistent physical warmth throughout the day

currency.text: When I think about what makes me feel truly seen by another person, it is:

options.a: When they articulate back to me what they see and value in me
options.b: When they notice what I need and just handle it
options.c: When they remember something meaningful and mark it with a gesture
options.d: When they set aside everything else to just be with me
options.e: When they are warm, close, and physically present with me

currency.text: When I think about a moment I felt deeply loved in the past, it was because:

options.a: Someone told me something about me that I had never heard said that clearly
options.b: Someone quietly took care of me without making it a big deal
options.c: I received a gift that was so specific to me it felt like they truly knew me
options.d: We had time together that was completely uninterrupted and just real
options.e: There was warmth and physical connection that made me feel held

currency.text: After an argument or a hard conversation, I feel most reconciled when:

options.a: We talk it through and they tell me clearly where we stand
options.b: They do something caring to show we are okay
options.c: They bring me something or do a gesture to mark the repair
options.d: We spend quality time together that feels normal again
options.e: We hug it out and physically reconnect

currency.text: When I imagine the perfect way someone shows they are thinking of me, it is:

options.a: A message that says exactly why I came to their mind
options.b: They handled something for me before I even thought to ask
options.c: They picked up something small that reminded them of me
options.d: They blocked off time for us before anything else filled the calendar
options.e: They reached for my hand or leaned into me when we were together

currency.text: When I am proud of myself, the kind of validation that means the most is:

options.a: Someone naming exactly what they see and why it matters
options.b: Someone taking something off my hands so I can enjoy the moment
options.c: A meaningful token or keepsake to remember the moment
options.d: Someone carving out time to hear all about it
options.e: A celebratory hug or physical expression of joy

currency.text: The thing that makes me feel safest and most secure in a close relationship is:

options.a: Knowing words of love and appreciation are freely and often spoken
options.b: Knowing the person will show up and handle things when it matters
options.c: Receiving intentional gestures that show I was in their thoughts
options.d: Having regular, unhurried time together that we both protect
options.e: Having physical closeness and warmth as a consistent part of how we connect

channel.text: When learning something new, I prefer to:

options.a: Watch a demonstration or study diagrams and visuals
options.b: Listen to an explanation or talk it through with someone
options.c: Read the instructions or find articles to study
options.d: Try it myself and learn as I go

channel.text: When I am trying to remember something important, I:

options.a: Visualize it in my mind or picture where I saw it
options.b: Repeat it out loud or talk through it with myself
options.c: Write it down or make a list
options.d: Associate it with something I have physically done

channel.text: When I am working through a complex problem, I:

options.a: Draw it out or map it visually
options.b: Talk through it out loud or call someone to think out loud
options.c: Write out the details and analyze them on paper
options.d: Start experimenting and figure it out through action

channel.text: When I receive directions to somewhere new, I prefer:

options.a: A map or a visual layout I can reference
options.b: Someone telling me the directions step by step
options.c: Written turn-by-turn directions I can read
options.d: Just going and figuring it out as I navigate

channel.text: When I want to explain something clearly to someone else, I tend to:

options.a: Show them visually, draw a picture, or use examples they can see
options.b: Talk them through it and check in as I go
options.c: Write it out so they can read and refer back to it
options.d: Walk them through the process by doing it together

channel.text: When studying or preparing for something important, I:

options.a: Use charts, color-coding, or visual summaries
options.b: Listen to recordings or talk through the material
options.c: Take detailed notes and review them in writing
options.d: Practice by actually doing it repeatedly

channel.text: When I am distracted or losing focus, it is usually because:

options.a: My environment has too much visual clutter or motion
options.b: There is too much background noise or talking around me
options.c: I do not have a clear summary or written reference to follow
options.d: I have been sitting still for too long without doing something

channel.text: When I am attending a presentation or training, I get the most out of it when:

options.a: There are slides, visuals, and well-designed graphics
options.b: The speaker is engaging and explains things conversationally
options.c: There is a handout or written material I can follow along with
options.d: There are activities, exercises, or hands-on components

channel.text: When I am processing how I feel about something, I:

options.a: Think in images and scenes, picturing the situation
options.b: Talk through it out loud to someone I trust
options.c: Journal or write about it to get my thoughts clear
options.d: Go for a walk, exercise, or do something physical to process it

channel.text: When I am bored in a conversation or meeting, it is usually because:

options.a: There is nothing to look at, reference, or see on screen
options.b: The person is speaking in a monotone or unclear way
options.c: There is no written agenda or materials to reference
options.d: We are just talking and not doing or building anything

channel.text: When making an important decision, I:

options.a: Create a visual layout or comparison chart
options.b: Talk it through with someone whose opinion I value
options.c: Make a written pros-and-cons list and review it
options.d: Go with my gut, informed by what I have experienced firsthand

channel.text: When I want to share an idea, I usually:

options.a: Sketch it out or put together something visual to show
options.b: Call or voice message someone to talk through it
options.c: Send a detailed written message or email laying it all out
options.d: Jump in and start building a prototype or draft version

channel.text: When I need to master a new skill quickly, I:

options.a: Find a video tutorial and watch someone do it well
options.b: Find a podcast, audio course, or someone to explain it to me
options.c: Find a well-written guide and read it thoroughly
options.d: Get my hands on it and start practicing immediately

channel.text: When I am communicating an update or status to others, I prefer to:

options.a: Present it visually, with a slide or a visual summary
options.b: Walk them through it verbally in a quick conversation
options.c: Send a written update they can read at their own pace
options.d: Do a live walkthrough of what has actually been built

channel.text: My ideal workspace or environment for deep focus is:

options.a: Visually clean and organized, with clear sight lines
options.b: Quiet enough that I can think clearly or use background sound intentionally
options.c: Set up so I can write, take notes, and have my reference materials nearby
options.d: A place where I can move around, stand, or shift positions as I work

channel.text: When I want to remember a conversation or meeting, I:

options.a: Recall the faces, the room, and what I was looking at
options.b: Replay the words and tone of what was said
options.c: Refer back to the notes I wrote during or after
options.d: Remember how I felt and what I was doing physically at the time

channel.text: When I get feedback on something I created, I absorb it best when:

options.a: I can see the edits or markups directly on the work
options.b: The person talks me through it conversationally
options.c: It comes in written form I can review and revisit
options.d: We sit down and rework it together in real time

channel.text: When I have an important message to communicate to someone, I feel most confident when I:

options.a: Have a visual, a slide, or something concrete to show them
options.b: Tell them in person or by phone so I can use my voice and tone
options.c: Write it out fully so every word is exactly right
options.d: Show them through action or walk them through an experience

compass.text: When I think about what gives my life the most meaning, it is:

options.a: My spiritual practice, beliefs, and connection to something greater
options.b: The people closest to me and the bonds I share with them
options.c: The work I do and the impact I create through it
options.d: Being part of a broader community and contributing to something larger

compass.text: When I have to make a major life decision, I am most guided by:

options.a: My convictions, prayer, or a sense of inner calling
options.b: What is best for the people I love most
options.c: What aligns with my professional goals and long-term vision
options.d: What will be best for my neighborhood, city, or larger group

compass.text: On a free weekend with no obligations, I am most likely to spend it:

options.a: In spiritual practice, reflection, worship, or personal growth
options.b: With close family or the people I consider home
options.c: Working on something meaningful or building toward a goal
options.d: Attending community events or investing in collective gatherings

compass.text: When I feel most like myself, it is usually when I am:

options.a: Aligned spiritually and living from a place of conviction
options.b: Deeply connected to and at peace with the people I love
options.c: Doing work that challenges and fulfills me
options.d: Contributing to something that serves more than just myself

compass.text: When I am feeling lost or off-track, I tend to find myself by:

options.a: Returning to my spiritual foundation and practices
options.b: Reconnecting with the people who know me best
options.c: Getting clear on my purpose and what I am building
options.d: Plugging back into my community and finding where I can give

compass.text: The accomplishment I would be most proud of at the end of my life is:

options.a: Having lived faithfully according to my deepest convictions
options.b: Having loved and raised a family that is healthy and whole
options.c: Having built something meaningful that outlasts me
options.d: Having made my community or the world genuinely better

compass.text: When I volunteer my time, I am most drawn to causes involving:

options.a: Spiritual development, discipleship, or helping people find meaning
options.b: Supporting families, children, or people in vulnerable home situations
options.c: Mentoring professionals or supporting economic development
options.d: Neighborhood improvement, civic engagement, or collective well-being

compass.text: When I think about where I draw my strength from, it is most often:

options.a: My faith, spiritual disciplines, and relationship with the divine
options.b: The love and support of my family and closest relationships
options.c: My sense of purpose and the progress I see in my work
options.d: The energy I get from being part of a group working toward something good

compass.text: When I think about what I most want to pass on to the next generation, it is:

options.a: A strong spiritual foundation and sense of calling
options.b: A deep sense of family identity, love, and belonging
options.c: A work ethic and the tools to build a meaningful life
options.d: A heart for others and a commitment to collective responsibility

compass.text: The kind of person I most admire is someone who:

options.a: Lives with deep integrity and spiritual authenticity
options.b: Has built a thriving, loving family and close relationships
options.c: Has achieved meaningful success and left a lasting professional legacy
options.d: Has dedicated their life to serving and uplifting those around them

compass.text: When something goes wrong in my life, my first instinct is to:

options.a: Seek guidance through prayer, meditation, or spiritual counsel
options.b: Talk to the people closest to me who know my heart
options.c: Problem-solve and find the most strategic path forward
options.d: Reach out to my broader network and find collective support

compass.text: When I look at how I spend my energy most consistently, it is on:

options.a: My spiritual life and growth
options.b: The people who are closest to me
options.c: My work, projects, and professional development
options.d: Groups, organizations, and the needs of those around me

compass.text: If I had to choose one thing I cannot compromise on, it would be:

options.a: Living in alignment with my spiritual values and convictions
options.b: Protecting and prioritizing the people I call family
options.c: Pursuing work that I find meaningful and that allows me to grow
options.d: Staying invested in and connected to my community

compass.text: The best version of my daily life includes:

options.a: Time for spiritual practice, reflection, and grounding
options.b: Deep, unhurried connection with the people I love most
options.c: Progress on work that is meaningful and building toward something
options.d: Moments of contribution, connection, and service to others

compass.text: When I am investing in myself, I feel most energized by:

options.a: Deepening my spiritual understanding and inner life
options.b: Becoming a better partner, parent, or family member
options.c: Developing skills and expertise that sharpen my work
options.d: Learning how to be a more effective contributor to my community

compass.text: When I am at my lowest, what pulls me back toward hope is:

options.a: My faith and the belief that my life has purpose beyond what I can see
options.b: The faces of the people who love me and need me
options.c: The vision of what I am building and why it matters
options.d: The awareness that I belong to something bigger than myself

compass.text: When I describe what I value most, the conversation naturally turns to:

options.a: Belief, calling, purpose, and the things that cannot be seen
options.b: Relationships, bonds, loyalty, and the people who matter most
options.c: Work, goals, growth, and building something that lasts
options.d: People, neighborhoods, belonging, and collective impact

compass.text: When I sacrifice something for the greater good, it is most likely for:

options.a: Living out a conviction I believe in deeply
options.b: Someone I love who needs me
options.c: A goal or project that is truly meaningful to me
options.d: A cause or group that is bigger than my own interests

compass.text: When I am making financial decisions, I am most influenced by:

options.a: My values around generosity, tithing, or spiritual stewardship
options.b: What is best for my household and the people depending on me
options.c: What will help me reach my professional and long-term goals
options.d: What I can give back or invest in causes beyond myself

compass.text: If I imagine the life I want ten years from now, the most non-negotiable part is:

options.a: Living with deep spiritual integrity and a clear sense of calling
options.b: Having rich, close relationships with the people I call family
options.c: Having built work or a legacy I am genuinely proud of
options.d: Being embedded in a community where I am known, loved, and contributing

partnership.text: When a romantic relationship is new, I tend to:

options.a: Move things forward and create opportunities to connect
options.b: Take my cues from the other person and match their energy
options.c: Ensure we are building something stable and mutual from the start
options.d: Go with the flow and let it develop naturally

partnership.text: When planning time together with a partner, I am most likely to:

options.a: Initiate and plan something specific
options.b: Wait to see what they want and make it happen for them
options.c: Suggest we take turns planning so it feels equal
options.d: Be open to whatever and make the most of it

partnership.text: When we have not connected in a while, I:

options.a: Reach out first and make something happen
options.b: Wait for them to reach out but respond enthusiastically
options.c: Notice the gap and bring it up so we can be intentional
options.d: Let it happen organically whenever our schedules align

partnership.text: When a partner expresses a need, I:

options.a: Often anticipated it before they said it and was already moving
options.b: Listen carefully and respond to exactly what they asked for
options.c: Make sure my needs and theirs are both on the table
options.d: Stay flexible and show up however they need me to

partnership.text: In conversations about the future of the relationship, I tend to:

options.a: Bring it up and lead the conversation
options.b: Follow their lead and share my thoughts when asked
options.c: Make sure we are both equally heard and considered
options.d: Stay open and see where the conversation goes

partnership.text: When conflict arises in a relationship, I typically:

options.a: Address it directly and push to resolve it
options.b: Respond to what my partner brings to me and follow their pace
options.c: Name the issue and make sure both sides are heard fairly
options.d: Stay calm, stay flexible, and work with whatever approach helps

partnership.text: In a healthy relationship, my natural role is:

options.a: The one who sets the direction and creates momentum
options.b: The one who supports and uplifts whatever direction we take
options.c: The one who keeps things fair, equal, and sustainable
options.d: The one who adjusts to what the relationship needs in any season

partnership.text: When showing love to a partner, I am most inclined to:

options.a: Surprise them with something I planned
options.b: Give them exactly what they asked for or expressed needing
options.c: Make sure our love is expressed in ways that feel equal and consistent
options.d: Show up differently depending on what each moment calls for

partnership.text: When making decisions as a couple, I tend to:

options.a: Bring a proposal and be ready to lead the process
options.b: Hear what my partner thinks first and work from there
options.c: Make sure we arrive at a decision together and both own it
options.d: Stay open to any outcome and make peace with what we decide

partnership.text: When my partner is going through something difficult, I:

options.a: Step in, take action, and try to fix or solve it for them
options.b: Ask what they need and deliver exactly that
options.c: Check that I am carrying my share of the weight during that season
options.d: Adjust fully to whatever they need, even if it shifts day to day

partnership.text: When I think about what I bring to a romantic relationship, it is:

options.a: Energy, direction, and the willingness to pursue
options.b: Attentiveness, responsiveness, and the ability to meet my partner where they are
options.c: Fairness, consistency, and the desire to keep things healthy for both of us
options.d: Flexibility, peace, and the ability to make any situation work

partnership.text: When planning a meaningful experience for a partner, I:

options.a: Come up with the idea, plan it, and make it happen
options.b: Ask what they would love and build the experience around that
options.c: Plan something that honors both our preferences equally
options.d: Let it evolve and find the magic in wherever the day takes us

partnership.text: When I sense something is off between us, I:

options.a: Name it and call for a conversation
options.b: Wait to see if they bring it up and respond from there
options.c: Find a way to surface it that feels fair to both of us
options.d: Stay patient and let things settle before deciding whether to address it

partnership.text: When my partner wants to try something new or different, I:

options.a: Have already thought of it and was about to suggest it
options.b: Happily go along and support what they want to explore
options.c: Evaluate whether it feels right for both of us before committing
options.d: Say yes with an open mind and figure it out as we go

partnership.text: In a season where the relationship needs extra attention, I:

options.a: Take the lead in creating more intentional connection
options.b: Follow my partner's pace and meet whatever level of attention they are seeking
options.c: Make sure the investment feels mutual and sustainable
options.d: Lean into whatever the relationship needs without needing a structured approach

partnership.text: When we are together but both have been busy, I:

options.a: Create an intentional moment to reconnect
